GET TO KNOW YOUR AI MARKETING TEAM

You set the direction.
Clara keeps it moving.

Start with your product knowledge, explore ideas in chat, and create content with Plays. Bring pieces together in campaigns, delegate recurring work to agents, and use the planner to decide what comes next—with the level of autonomy you choose.

Get early access ↗
01 / BRING YOUR WORLD

The best starting point?
What you already know.

Add the sources that explain your product: documentation, GitHub repositories, websites, or uploaded files. Clara builds a knowledge base from configured sources and uses relevant context when drafting.

Product context

Keep each product’s knowledge together so a new brief can start from the right material.

A recognizable voice

Define your brand’s audience, voice, and writing rules, with product-specific guidance where needed.

Your own methods

Add reusable skills to capture approaches and instructions your team wants Clara to use.

Keep the sources current. Source-backed drafting helps ground the work, but your review still matters.
02 / START THE CONVERSATION

Say what you’re
trying to say.

Start in chat or choose a content play. Explain what changed, who it matters to, and what you want to create. Clara uses the brief and relevant product context to draft the work.

“Turn this release into a LinkedIn post and an article for product teams. Keep it practical, and show what’s changed for the user.”

Example brief. Your actual result depends on the context and provider you configure.

One idea, one piece

Create a post, article, X thread, or release announcement for a specific audience and channel.

A connected campaign

Start from a product launch or version release playbook to organize related pieces around the same story.

Explore the content examples ↗
03 / GIVE IT ANOTHER DIMENSION

Some ideas
need to be seen.

Go beyond a text draft with Clara’s visual creation tools.

▧

Carousels

Create LinkedIn PDFs and Instagram image sets. Bring screenshots and terminal visuals into a story that unfolds slide by slide.

▷

Video studio

Start from a brief and uploaded footage, images, or audio. Review a rendered preview, ask for revisions, and export an approved MP4.

Video creation needs a configured rendering service and AI provider.
04 / CONNECT THE STEPS

Your process.
Built on a canvas.

Open Workflows to build an automation on the visual canvas. Add blocks, connect their inputs and outputs, and select each step to edit its properties. Combine research, content creation, decisions, review, and publication planning. Build with blocks or describe the sequence through Build with Clara.

Branch and bring work together

Use parallel paths for an article and social content, conditions for different outcomes, and loops for a list of items. A step with several incoming connections waits for its dependencies.

Choose the trigger

Run when you ask, on a schedule, from a Clara event, or through a configured webhook. Choose timing and timezone in the Trigger step.

See what happened

Follow runs and outputs in Activity, and manage planned posts in Calendar. Pause an agent or an individual job when the plan changes.

Explore the workflow canvas ↗
A trigger starts the work; it does not promise an immediate publication. Generation, approvals, connected accounts, and your publishing schedule still determine when content goes live.
05 / GIVE YOUR TEAM ITS JOBS

Agents have a role.
Workflows make it happen.

Open Agents to choose from the Agent library or build your own. Give an agent a goal, standing instructions, and one or more jobs. Each job is a workflow with its own steps, start rules, and activity history.

Your marketing specialists

Start with Content Writer, Social Manager, Search Visibility, or Competitor Analyst. Each comes with jobs you can inspect and adapt to your product.

One agent, several jobs

A Social Manager can plan the week, fill calendar gaps, and repurpose published posts. Shared instructions and learning carry across its jobs.

Workflows in their own right

Open Workflows to build and manage repeatable sequences, including workflows that run independently of an agent.

06 / PLANNER & CALENDAR

Plan the work.
See it on Calendar.

Clara’s marketing planner brings together your priorities, product context, market signals, and what your agents have learned. It proposes objectives and books suitable jobs for your enabled agents on Calendar.

Set your priorities

Use Talk to Clara in Calendar’s Plan view to explain what matters now. Your guidance shapes the next plan, alongside available search data, competitor observations, and previous results.

See your schedule on Calendar

Scheduled posts and agent jobs share one calendar. Review upcoming work and its status, schedule a draft, or move a booking. Each planner objective names an agent, a job, and a brief you can edit; reject work with a reason to guide the next plan.

Learn and plan again

Clara plans weekly, and you can request a new plan when priorities change. Feedback and agent lessons inform the next plan; existing bookings and your edits are preserved.

Calendar bookings show when work starts. Publishing follows the job’s workflow, approvals, and connected channels. Autonomy settings, guardrails, and the run budget still apply.
07 / CHOOSE HOW MUCH TO DELEGATE

Your marketing team.
Ready for Autopilot.

In Settings → Autonomy, choose what Clara may do on its own. These presets govern automatic actions; your guardrails and the creator’s permissions always apply.

Assistant

Clara suggests work. Nothing runs on its own.

Co-pilot

Internal work can run automatically. External or irreversible actions, including publishing, ask for approval.

Autopilot

Work can run automatically, publishing included. Keep a person in the loop with approval overrides for an action, channel, or product.

Set posting limits, quiet hours, and topics to avoid. Agent restrictions can be stricter than the workspace preset, and newly set-up agents may still wait for approval. Pause Autopilot whenever you need to.
